fact: Article 11 of loi n° 05-20 on cybersecurity (dahir n° 1-20-69 of 25 July 2020, Bulletin officiel n° 6906 of 6 August 2020) requires sensitive data to be hosted exclusively on national territory, with fines of 200,000 to 400,000 DH under article 49 for heads of vital entities or infrastructures hosting it abroad; article 53 makes the law operative only on publication of its implementing texts.
system: Loi n° 05-20 relative à la cybersécurité, article 11

fact: Hespress English, citing a Global Finance report, states that a 2021 law mandates sensitive data be stored locally in Morocco; the date is the article's published date, and the article gives no law name.
system: 2021 law mandating local storage of sensitive data (unnamed)

fact: The Maroc IA 2030 portfolio presented on 8 September 2026 includes a 50 MW data centre in Rabat associated with a sovereign cloud and a 'Move to Cloud' programme for public administrations.

Minister Seghrouchni said the cloud roadmap's second objective is a secure, ordered move of public data to the cloud, in line with national data protection law and qualified providers, including a national sovereign cloud infrastructure for the state's sensitive information systems.
The minister said on 1 December 2025 that the Cloud 2025-2030 roadmap, through the Cloud First Policy under Digital Morocco 2030, will strengthen the country's digital sovereignty.

LesEco reports Morocco's Cloud Strategy 2025-2030 and Cloud First Policy, a circular-backed default for public administrations within Digital Morocco 2030, are presented as pillars of digital sovereignty.
